title: Replace a Number, Sum a Range

concept.title: An assignment is an addition of the difference between the new and the old value
body: A Fenwick tree knows only how to **add** to a position. This time the operations **replace** a number by a given value. For the row `3 8 1` the sum of all cells is 12; after replacing the cell 2 by 0 it is 4. To use the tree for this, remember the **current value** of each cell in a plain array `cur`.

Replacing the value `cur[x]` by `y` changes every sum that contains the position `x` by `y - cur[x]`. So an assignment is just an **addition of the difference**: `add(x, y - cur[x])`, followed by `cur[x] = y`. If the new value is equal to the old one, the difference is 0 and nothing changes. Range sums are answered as before, with two prefix sums.
The same trick turns every "set" operation on an additive structure (a Fenwick tree, a prefix table) into an "add" operation. Each operation costs O(log n), and the extra array costs O(n) memory.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` replaces the number at the position `x` by `y`; type 2 `x y` asks for the sum of the numbers at the positions `x` to `y`. Print the answers to all the questions of type 2 on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the sum of the cells from `x` to `y`.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for a sum 1 <= x <= y <= n.
hints: A Fenwick tree adds; to replace a value, add the difference.
Keep the current value of every cell in an array.
Sums are still the difference of two prefix sums.

a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: The tree stores the sums; a replacement adds the difference between the new and the current value of the cell, and range sums are differences of prefix sums.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def bit_add(t, i, x):
    n = len(t) - 1
    while i <= n:
        t[i] += x
        i += i & -i

def bit_sum(t, i):
    s = 0
    while i > 0:
        s += t[i]
        i -= i & -i
    return s

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

t = [0] * (n + 1)
cur = a[:]
for i in range(n):
    bit_add(t, i + 1, a[i])
out = []
for kind, x, y in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        bit_add(t, x, y - cur[x - 1])
        cur[x - 1] = y
    else:
        out.append(bit_sum(t, y) - bit_sum(t, x - 1))
print(*out)
